claim_1.claim: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of platelet-rich plasma from young, Older (Comm), and Older (SNF) adults at Day 0, Day 2, Day 7, and Day 28 post-vaccination showed age-associated increases in platelet activation RNAs and mitochondrial genes, and decreases in translation-related RNAs.

sources.quote: Overall, pre‐vaccination RNA expression variability was most highly associated with group membership, and there was a continuum of transcriptional states moving from Young to Older (Comm) to Older (SNF) adults.
In contrast to the age‐associated increase in platelet activation RNAs, RNAs in pathways related to translation decreased with age and SNF resident status.

claim_2.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of platelet-rich plasma from young, Older (Comm), and Older (SNF) adults at Day 0, Day 2, and Day 7 post-vaccination showed increased surface expression of CD62p, CD40L, and CD63 in Older (Comm) compared to young adults, with decreased expression in Older (SNF) compared to Older (Comm).

sources.quote: The levels of surface expression of all three proteins were significantly increased in platelets from Older (Comm), compared to young adults at day 0, 2, and 7, suggesting an age‐associated increase in platelet activation.

claim_3.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition analysis of serum from young and older adults at Day 0 and Day 28 post-vaccination showed classification of high and low vaccine responders using maxRBA, with differential RNA expression in high responders.

sources.quote: Influenza vaccine antibody response was measured using a standard hemagglutination inhibition assay (HAI).
maxRBA was used to classify high and low vaccine responders for assessment of platelet transcriptomic differences in vaccine responsiveness.
